issues.legal_issue: A part of a building previously let remains premises capable of requisition even when the landlord obtains possession to occupy it personally.
material_facts: The room was a part of a larger building and had previously been let to a tenant.
The landlords obtained possession after an eviction decree that included their bona fide requirement to occupy the room.
issues.conclusion: The room was premises within the statutory definition and could be requisitioned; the landlords’ intention to occupy it after eviction did not change that status.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(3) of the Bombay Land Requisition Act, 1948, “let or intended to be let separately” applies to a part of a building, not to an entire building. A part of a building falls within the definition if it was let or intended to be let separately when the Act came into force; a later change in the landlord’s intention does not remove it from the definition.

predicates.requisition_challenge: A party challenged whether premises could be requisitioned.
predicates.part_of_building: The premises at issue formed part of a larger building.
predicates.part_was_let_at_commencement: The part of the building had been let when the requisition law came into force.
predicates.part_was_intended_to_be_let_at_commencem: The part of the building was intended to be let separately when the requisition law came into force.
predicates.part_qualifies_as_requisitionable_premis: The part of the building falls within the category of premises that may be requisitioned.

issues.definition: When a requisition challenge concerns a part of a building that was let or intended to be let separately when the law came into force, that part qualifies as premises capable of requisition.

issues.legal_issue: Premises made vacant by a court-ordered eviction for the landlord’s occupation may be requisitioned for a public purpose and allotted to a homeless person.
material_facts: The landlords obtained possession through execution of an eviction decree, which included their bona fide requirement to occupy the room.
The former occupant applied to the accommodation authority for requisition and allotment, stating that he had no other accommodation.
The government requisitioned the room for the public purpose of housing a homeless person and allotted it to the former occupant.
The Requisition Act was enacted after the Rent Act and did not exclude premises made vacant by an eviction on the ground of the landlord’s requirement.
issues.conclusion: The requisition and allotment were not invalid merely because the room became vacant after an eviction decree based on the landlords’ need to occupy it; there was no conflict between the relevant provisions of the two Acts.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6(1) and 6(4) of the Bombay Land Requisition Act, 1948 permit requisition of premises that become vacant upon a tenant’s eviction, for a public purpose. Under The State of Bombay v. Bhanji Munji, requisitioning premises to house a homeless person serves a public purpose. Sections 13 and 17 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 do not prevent such requisition: the Acts address different matters, the later Requisition Act contains no exception for this kind of eviction, and non-occupation required by the requisition law may be for reasonable cause under the Rent Act.

rule.if: requisition_challenge and vacancy_followed_court_ordered_eviction and eviction_included_landlord_occupation_need and government_requisitioned_for_public_housing and allottee_was_homeless

predicates.requisition_challenge: A party challenged a government requisition and the related allotment.
predicates.vacancy_followed_court_ordered_eviction: The premises became vacant after a court-ordered eviction.
predicates.eviction_included_landlord_occupation_ne: The grounds for the eviction included the landlord’s need to occupy the premises.
predicates.government_requisitioned_for_public_hous: The government requisitioned the premises to provide housing as a public purpose.
predicates.allottee_was_homeless: The person to whom the premises were allotted had no other accommodation.
predicates.requisition_and_allotment_are_not_invali: The eviction ground and subsequent allotment do not, by themselves, invalidate the requisition or allotment.

issues.definition: When a requisition challenge concerns a vacancy following a court-ordered eviction that included the landlord’s occupation need, requisition for public housing and allotment to a homeless person are not invalid on that basis.

issues.legal_issue: An allotment to a former occupant is not mala fide merely because that occupant had been evicted and had acted improperly toward the landlord.
material_facts: The allottee had occupied the room before eviction, had not paid rent to the landlords, and had taken steps that delayed execution of the eviction decree.
The allottee applied for the room the day after eviction.
There was no finding that the government acted from animus against the landlords or used requisition for a purpose outside the Act.
issues.conclusion: Those circumstances did not make the requisition order mala fide in law in the absence of animus against the landlords or an unauthorized purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(4) of the Bombay Land Requisition Act, 1948 authorizes requisition for a public purpose. Under The State of Bombay v. Bhanji Munji, requisition to house a homeless person may serve that purpose. The allottee’s prior occupation, conduct toward the landlord, and prompt application do not establish mala fides where the order was not motivated by animus or made for a purpose for which requisition could not be used.

rule.if: requisition_challenge and allottee_was_previously_evicted_from_premises and allottee_had_prior_rent_or_execution_misconduct and allottee_applied_promptly and government_lacked_animus_against_owner and government_used_power_for_authorized_purpose

predicates.requisition_challenge: A party challenged a government requisition as mala fide.
predicates.allottee_was_previously_evicted_from_pre: The person allotted the premises had previously been evicted from them.
predicates.allottee_had_prior_rent_or_execution_mis: The allottee had failed to pay rent or had obstructed or delayed execution of the eviction decree.
predicates.allottee_applied_promptly: The allottee applied for the premises soon after being evicted.
predicates.government_lacked_animus_against_owner: The government did not act out of personal hostility toward the owner.
predicates.government_used_power_for_authorized_pur: The government used requisition for a purpose for which the power could lawfully be exercised.
predicates.requisition_is_not_mala_fide: The requisition is not legally mala fide on the stated facts.

issues.definition: Even where a former occupant had misconducted himself toward the owner and applied promptly after eviction, the requisition is not mala fide if the government lacked animus and acted for an authorized purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A declaration in a requisition order that premises were vacant is conclusive evidence of vacancy when the landlord did not give notice of the vacancy.
material_facts: The landlords did not give the prescribed intimation of vacancy.
The government made an inquiry and declared in the requisition order that the premises had become vacant.
The landlords disputed that the premises were vacant when requisitioned.
issues.conclusion: The landlords could not successfully dispute vacancy because the declaration in the requisition order was conclusive evidence of it.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 6(4)(a) and its proviso of the Bombay Land Requisition Act, 1948, where the landlord has not given the prescribed intimation, the government must make such inquiry as it deems fit and declare in the requisition order that the premises were or had become vacant; that declaration is conclusive evidence of vacancy. Section 6(1) and its explanation address when premises become vacant, including when a tenant ceases to occupy them by eviction.

rule.if: requisition_challenge and landlord_did_not_report_vacancy and government_inquired_into_vacancy and requisition_order_declared_vacancy

predicates.requisition_challenge: A party challenged a requisition on the ground that the premises were not vacant.
predicates.landlord_did_not_report_vacancy: The landlord did not give the prescribed notice that the premises had become vacant.
predicates.government_inquired_into_vacancy: The government made an inquiry into whether the premises were vacant.
predicates.requisition_order_declared_vacancy: The requisition order declared that the premises were or had become vacant.
predicates.vacancy_is_conclusively_established: The premises’ vacancy is treated as conclusively established.

issues.definition: If the landlord did not report a vacancy and the government inquired and declared vacancy in its requisition order, vacancy is conclusively established.

issues.legal_issue: A writ petition seeking to quash an allotment order is not maintainable when the person to whom the premises were allotted is not a party.
material_facts: The landlords sought writ relief to quash both the requisition order and the allotment order.
The person to whom the room had been allotted was not joined as a party to the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The allottee’s absence from the proceedings was fatal to the maintainability of the writ petition.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a writ petition seeking to quash an allotment to a person cannot be maintained when that allottee is not a party to the proceedings.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_allotment: A party brought a writ petition seeking to quash an allotment of premises.
predicates.allottee_not_joined_as_party: The person to whom the premises were allotted was not made a party to the writ proceedings.
predicates.writ_petition_is_not_maintainable: The writ petition cannot be maintained.

issues.definition: A writ petition challenging an allotment cannot be maintained when the person who received the allotment was not joined as a party.
